title: Imaging the Waltz of Atoms: Initial Results and Challenges of Detecting Circularly Polarized Phonons in STEM-EELS
content: Phonons, the quasi-particle associated with quanta of vibrational excitations in solids, are routinely studied in Electron Energy Loss Spectroscopy (EELS) in Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopes (STEMs) equipped with monochromators capable of reaching sub-10 meV energy resolution [1]. As wave excitations, phonons are characterized by a wave vector k, which determines the propagation direction of the wave and is inversely related to the wave length λ, a band index ν and a frequency ωkν. Furthermore, a characteristic displacement pattern of atoms in the crystal, known as the phonon polarization ekν, is associated with each phonon mode (k,ν). If all three component of the polarization vector ekν are real numbers, the motion of atoms associated with the phonon mode (k,ν) follows a linear oscillation trajectory. However, if the polarization vector ekν becomes complex, the motion of atoms traces an elliptic or circular path in mode (k,ν). Like dancers in a ball room, each atom undergoes a rotational motion around its equilibrium position in this Waltz of Atoms and the corresponding phonon mode is said to be circularly polarized.
